svg.aria-label: Animated map of 32 shared-memory banks, where bank = column mod 32, during one 16-byte read of row k of B's tile by the first 8 threads. Each row of cells is 32 columns, so columns 0, 32, 64 and 96 share bank 0. Before: each thread owns 8 contiguous columns, so thread starts are 8 columns apart (t0 at column 0, t1 at 8, up to t7 at 56). Thread 4 starts at column 32, which wraps onto thread 0's banks; every used bank serves 2 threads, half the banks sit idle, and the read takes 2 passes. After: each thread's 8 columns are split into two groups of 4, so thread starts are 4 columns apart (t0 at 0, t1 at 4, up to t7 at 28). 8 threads times 4 columns is 32 consecutive columns, so every bank serves exactly one thread: 1 pass. Threads 8 to 15 take columns 32 to 63 with their first groups, so the second groups start at column 64. That second read is a separate instruction with its own pass; since 64 mod 32 = 0 it reuses the same banks, one thread each, but at a different time.
svg.text: A 16-byte read of row k of B’s tile: which banks do the first 8 threads hit?
two groups of 4 columns per thread
Row k of B’s tile is 128 floats and wraps around the 32 banks 4 times.
Each thread reads its 8 columns as two 16-byte reads, 4 columns each.
First read: with neighbors 8 columns apart, 8 threads span 64 columns.
Columns 32–63 reuse banks 0–31: t4 collides with t0, t5 with t1, and so on.
With 2 threads on each used bank, the read takes 2 passes.
First read: neighbors now start 4 columns apart, not 8.
One thread per bank: the read takes 1 pass.
Threads 8–15 take columns 32–63, in their own pass.
So second groups start at column 64.
Spacing neighbors 4 columns apart instead of 8 is what removes the conflict.
